key_insight: Inserting a thin high work-function metal interlayer between ITO and NiOx lowers the hole-injection barrier and sharply boosts all-inorganic PeLED luminance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a simple, scalable anode-interface modification that can improve charge injection and device brightness without changing the core perovskite stack.
method: Drift-diffusion and Poisson equations were simulated in Setfos LED software.
A thin metal transition layer (e.g., 2 nm Au) was inserted between ITO and NiOx.
High work-function metals such as Au, Pd, and Pt were compared for hole-injection enhancement.
evidence_signal: Simulation results showed that a 2 nm Au interlayer increased luminance by more than 18×, with similar improvement trends for Pd and Pt.
watch_item: The findings are simulation-based, so practical gains will depend on film continuity, thickness control, and compatibility with fabrication and stability constraints.
paper_title: Boosting Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes Performance by Introducing High Work-function Metal Transition Layer
